options: A. Store your PFD under the foredeck, stand on the gunwale during a jibe, and swim away from the hull if the boat capsizes.
B. Tie the mainsheet in a hard knot to the cleat so your hands are free, and dive under the sail if the boat turtles.
C. Always wear a properly fitted USCG-approved PFD, watch for the boom swinging across the cockpit during tacks and especially jibes, and stay with the floating sailboat if it capsizes.
D. Remove the centerboard when sailing upwind in strong gusts so the boat cannot heel over.

requirements.lead_text: Following the Scouting America Safety Afloat plan, show that you and a buddy can sail a boat properly. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Following the Scouting America Safety Afloat plan, show that you and a buddy can sail a boat properly. Do the following: (a) Prepare a boat for sailing, including a safety inspection. (b) Get underway from a dock, mooring, or beach. (c) Properly set sails for a round-trip course approved by your counselor that will include running, beating, and reaching, the basic points of sail. While sailing, demonstrate good helmsmanship skills. (d) Change direction by tacking; change direction by jibing. (e) Demonstrate getting out of irons. (f) Demonstrate the safety position. (g) Demonstrate capsize procedures and the rescue of a person overboard. Note: Capsize procedures should be conducted under the close supervision of the counselor. A rescue boat should be standing by to assist, if necessary, and to tow the capsized craft to shore. Self-bailing boats are acceptable for this requirement. Extreme care should be taken to avoid personal injury and damage to the boat or equipment. (h) Demonstrate the procedure to take after running aground. (i) Accept a single line or side tow and maneuver the craft being towed safely for 20 boat lengths. (j) Upon returning to the dock, mooring, or beach, properly secure all equipment, furl or stow sails, and prepare the craft for unattended docking or beaching overnight or longer.

C. Always wear a properly fitted USCG-approved PFD, watch for the boom swinging across the cockpit during tacks and especially jibes, and stay with the floating sailboat if it capsizes.

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Sailing safety requires wearing a USCG-approved PFD at all times, keeping heads low and controlling the mainsheet when the boom crosses during tacks and jibes, and staying with a capsized hull.

D. The transom board located across the stern of the hull

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Ripples and darker patches of water (cat's-paws), onshore flags, mooring boats pointing into the breeze, and masthead wind indicators all reveal wind direction before you launch (p. 26).

C. Backing the jib or mainsail to one side and steering the rudder so the bow swings clear of the no-sail zone
D. Raising the centerboard completely out of the trunk and paddling backward toward the dock
choices: A. Pulling the mainsheet and jib sheet as tight as possible while keeping the rudder centered

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): When a boat is stuck in irons (pointed directly into the no-sail zone with zero headway), backing the jib or boom to one side while positioning the tiller lets the wind push the bow off the wind onto a tack (p. 31).
